subject: English

entries.question_text: Complete the sentence: When my friend arrived, I was about to —
entries.options_raw: a) be leaving b) leave c) left d) go
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Be about to + base verb' — 'about to leave' means on the point of leaving.

entries.question_text: Choose the correct sentence:

options.label: a
options.text: One of the most beautiful girls has come.

options.label: b
options.text: One of the most beautiful girl has come.

options.label: c
options.text: One of the most beautiful girls have come.

options.label: d
options.text: One of the beautiful girl are come.

entries.options_raw: a) One of the most beautiful girls has come. b) One of the most beautiful girl has come. c) One of the most beautiful girls have come. d) One of the beautiful girl are come.
entries.correct_answer: a) One of the most beautiful girls has come.
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'One of + plural noun + singular verb' — subject is 'One' (singular), so 'has'.

entries.question_text: Find out the correct synonym of 'hazard'.
entries.options_raw: a) Impartial b) Static c) Immobile d) Danger
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Hazard' = a source of danger or risk. Closest synonym is 'Danger'.

entries.question_text: Every day _____ begins at 9 O'clock and ends at 3 O'clock
entries.options_raw: a) college b) a college c) the college d) colleges
entries.explanation: Explanation: A specific college known to speaker/hearer requires the definite article 'the'.

entries.question_text: Which one is the correct passive form of the sentence 'Panic seized me'?
entries.options_raw: a) I was seized by panic b) I was seized for panic c) I was seized from panic d) I was seized with panic
entries.correct_answer: d) I was seized with panic
entries.explanation: Explanation: In the passive of emotional/mental-state verbs, 'with' is the standard preposition — 'seized with panic/fear/emotion'.

entries.question_text: I don't hanker ____ wealth.
entries.options_raw: a) for b) on c) over d) after
entries.explanation: Explanation: The verb 'hanker' takes the preposition 'after' — 'hanker after' = to have a strong desire for.

entries.question_text: Select the correct Bangla translation of 'It is a long story'.
entries.options_raw: ক) সে অনেক দিনের কথা খ) সে অনেক কথা গ) সে লম্বা গল্প করেছিল ঘ) সে অনেক বড় কথা বলেছিল
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'It is a long story' idiomatically = 'সে অনেক কথা' — বলার মতো অনেক কিছু আছে বোঝাতে।

entries.question_text: She could not but ____ there.
entries.options_raw: a) help going b) goes c) has gone d) go
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Could not but + base verb' = could not help + gerund — an alternative construction; here 'could not but go' means 'had to go / could not help going'.

entries.question_text: Noun of the word 'free' is —
entries.options_raw: a) freeness b) freely c) freedom d) freedomness
entries.explanation: Explanation: The standard noun form of 'free' is 'freedom'. 'Freely' is an adverb.

entries.question_text: 'Take one to tasks' means —
entries.options_raw: a) imitate b) rebuke c) resume d) restrain
entries.explanation: Explanation: The idiom 'take (someone) to task' = to reprimand/rebuke someone for a mistake.

entries.question_text: The dog was ____ in front of the door.
entries.options_raw: a) lain b) lying c) lied d) laid
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Lie' (intransitive, to recline) → present participle 'lying'. Past continuous 'was lying' fits perfectly.

entries.question_text: Which one is the correct English translation of 'এখন আমার হাত খালি'?
entries.options_raw: a) I am empty hand now b) I am empty pocket c) I am hard up now d) I am without money now
entries.correct_answer: c) I am hard up now
entries.explanation: Explanation: The idiom 'hard up' = short of money / in financial difficulty — matches 'হাত খালি'.

entries.question_text: The verb of 'sure' is —
entries.options_raw: a) surely b) surety c) ensure d) none of these
entries.explanation: Explanation: The verb form of 'sure' is 'ensure' (make certain). 'Surely' = adverb, 'surety' = noun.

entries.question_text: Rahim went to ____ hospital as patient.
entries.options_raw: a) the b) a c) an d) no article
entries.explanation: Explanation: When a person goes to an institution (hospital/school/church) for its primary purpose (treatment/study/worship), no article is used — 'go to hospital', 'go to school'.

entries.question_text: 'Writing is better than reading' — Negative form is —

options.label: a
options.text: Writing is not as good as reading

options.label: b
options.text: Reading is not as good as writing

options.label: c
options.text: Nothing is as good as writing

options.label: d
options.text: No other thing is as good as reading

entries.options_raw: a) Writing is not as good as reading b) Reading is not as good as writing c) Nothing is as good as writing d) No other thing is as good as reading
entries.correct_answer: b) Reading is not as good as writing
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'A is better than B' → 'B is not as good as A' — a standard positive-to-negative comparative transformation.

entries.question_text: It is high time we ____ our eating habits.
entries.options_raw: a) changed b) should change c) have changing d) change
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'It is high time + subject + past simple' — the subjunctive form expressing that an action is overdue.

entries.question_text: Select the correct Bangla translation of 'There is no room in the bench'.
entries.options_raw: ক) এ রুমে কোনো বেঞ্চ নেই খ) এ বেঞ্চে কোনো কক্ষ নেই গ) এ বেঞ্চে কোনো জায়গা নেই ঘ) কোথাও কোনো বেঞ্চ নেই
entries.correct_answer: গ) এ বেঞ্চে কোনো জায়গা নেই
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Room' এখানে 'কক্ষ' নয়, 'জায়গা/স্থান' অর্থে ব্যবহৃত হয়েছে। তাই 'বেঞ্চে জায়গা নেই'।

entries.question_text: 'শব্দটি কেটে দাও' এর শুদ্ধ ইংরেজি —
entries.options_raw: a) Pen through the word b) Cut the word c) Cut through the word d) Cut out the word
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Pen through' = to strike out (a word) with a pen — the idiomatic English expression for 'কেটে দাও'।

entries.question_text: What is the adjective of 'purify'?
entries.options_raw: a) Purity b) Pureful c) Pure d) Purifying
entries.explanation: Explanation: The base adjective form of 'purify' (verb) is 'pure'. 'Purity' = noun; 'Pureful' is not a standard word.

entries.question_text: We eat ____ we may live.
entries.options_raw: a) for b) because c) so that d) lest
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'So that + may/might + verb' expresses purpose — 'We eat so that we may live' = we eat in order to live.

entries.question_text: Which one is the correct passive form of the sentence 'I know you'?
entries.options_raw: a) You are known by me b) You are known to me c) You are unknown by me d) You are known with me
entries.correct_answer: b) You are known to me
entries.explanation: Explanation: In the passive of certain stative verbs ('know, help, please'), 'to' is the standard preposition — 'known to me'.

entries.question_text: Which one is a compound noun?
entries.options_raw: a) Comprehension b) Holiday c) Entertainment d) Hair-brush
entries.explanation: Explanation: A compound noun is formed by combining two or more words. 'Hair-brush' = hair + brush.

entries.question_text: Syntax is concerned with —
entries.options_raw: a) word b) letter c) passage d) sentence
entries.explanation: Explanation: Syntax = the branch of linguistics that deals with sentence structure — the arrangement of words to form sentences.

entries.question_text: Rana's father wants him to be an engineer ____ a doctor.
entries.options_raw: a) instead b) instead of c) expecting d) expect to
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Instead of + noun/gerund' is used to substitute one thing for another. 'An engineer instead of a doctor' = an engineer rather than a doctor.

entries.question_text: The correct spelling is —
entries.options_raw: a) humouros b) humourious c) humorous d) humorious
entries.explanation: Explanation: The standard American/British form is 'humorous' (adjective form of 'humour/humor').

entries.question_text: What is the adjective of 'child'?
entries.options_raw: a) Childhood b) Childly c) Childish d) Children
entries.explanation: Explanation: NTRCA কর্তৃপক্ষ প্রশ্নটি বাতিল করেছে। ('Child' has multiple valid adjective forms — 'childish' (negative) and 'childlike' (positive). Since only 'childish' appears in the options and 'childlike' is absent, the answer key was disputed and NTRCA cancelled the question.)

entries.question_text: The man is so weak that he cannot walk. (Simple)

options.label: a
options.text: The man is too weak to walk.

options.label: b
options.text: The man is so weak to walk.

options.label: c
options.text: The man is too weak for him to walk.

options.label: d
options.text: The man is so weak for him to walk

entries.options_raw: a) The man is too weak to walk. b) The man is so weak to walk. c) The man is too weak for him to walk. d) The man is so weak for him to walk
entries.correct_answer: a) The man is too weak to walk.
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'So…that + subject + cannot + verb' converts to 'too + adjective + to + verb' in the simple form.

entries.question_text: What have you bought? (Passive)

options.label: c
options.text: What are being bought by you?

options.label: d
options.text: What has been bought by you?

entries.options_raw: a) What are bought by you? b) What is bought by you? c) What are being bought by you? d) What has been bought by you?
entries.correct_answer: d) What has been bought by you?
entries.explanation: Explanation: Present perfect active 'have + past participle' → passive 'has/have + been + past participle'; the interrogative WH-word 'what' stays in front.

entries.question_text: Only Rina can do this sum. (Negative)

options.label: a
options.text: Only Rina cannot do this sum.

options.label: c
options.text: None but Rina can do this sum.

options.label: d
options.text: Any one but Rina can do this sum.

entries.options_raw: a) Only Rina cannot do this sum. b) Rina cannot do this sum. c) None but Rina can do this sum. d) Any one but Rina can do this sum.
entries.correct_answer: c) None but Rina can do this sum.
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Only + person' becomes 'None but + person' in the negative transformation.

entries.question_text: All love flower. (Interrogative)
entries.options_raw: a) Who does not love flower? b) Who do not love flower? c) Who did not love flower? d) Do all love flower?
entries.correct_answer: a) Who does not love flower?
entries.explanation: Explanation: A universal affirmative 'All love X' is turned into a rhetorical negative question 'Who does not love X?'.

entries.question_text: 'Cock and bull story' means —
entries.options_raw: a) a fable b) a tragedy c) a false story d) a wonderful story
entries.explanation: Explanation: The idiom 'cock and bull story' = an absurd, unbelievable, or false story.

entries.question_text: "Apple of one's eye" means —
entries.options_raw: a) extremely favorite b) apple like eye c) big eye d) apple coloured eye
entries.explanation: Explanation: The idiom 'apple of one's eye' = a person or thing that one loves most/dearly favourite.

entries.question_text: What is the meaning of 'white elephant'?

options.label: c
options.text: A very costly or troublesome possession

entries.options_raw: a) An elephant of white colour b) A black marketer c) A very costly or troublesome possession d) A hoarder
entries.correct_answer: c) A very costly or troublesome possession
entries.explanation: Explanation: The idiom 'white elephant' = a valuable but burdensome possession whose cost of upkeep is out of proportion to its usefulness.

entries.question_text: What a nice scenery it is! (Assertive)

options.label: b
options.text: It is a very nice scenery.

entries.options_raw: a) It is very nice scenery. b) It is a very nice scenery. c) It is a great scenery. d) The scenery is very nice.
entries.correct_answer: b) It is a very nice scenery.
entries.explanation: Explanation: Exclamatory 'What a + adjective + noun + it is!' → assertive 'It is a very + adjective + noun.' (NTRCA-approved form).

entries.question_text: Everybody should ________ their old parents.
entries.options_raw: a) look at b) look after c) look up d) look into
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Look after' = to take care of. Perfect fit for 'take care of old parents'.

entries.question_text: The patient will ______ soon.
entries.options_raw: a) come in b) come off c) come round d) come by
entries.explanation: Explanation: The phrasal verb 'come round' = to recover consciousness or good health.

entries.question_text: None of the students _______ a car.
entries.options_raw: a) have b) have got c) has d) own
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'None' as a singular indefinite pronoun (= not one) takes a singular verb in formal English.

entries.question_text: Would you mind ________ the window?
entries.options_raw: a) open b) to open c) to opening d) opening
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Mind' is always followed by a gerund (-ing form): 'Would you mind opening…'.

entries.question_text: You had better _____ a doctor.
entries.options_raw: a) to see b) see c) saw d) seen
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Had better' is always followed by the bare infinitive (base form) — 'had better see', 'had better go', etc.

entries.question_text: No sooner had the thief seen the police —
entries.options_raw: a) than he ran away b) than he run away c) than he had run away d) when he run away
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'No sooner had + past participle, than + past simple' is the standard correlative pattern.

entries.question_text: He is working hard —

options.label: a
options.text: as he can shine in life

options.label: b
options.text: that he can shine in life

options.label: d
options.text: so that he can shine in life

entries.options_raw: a) as he can shine in life b) that he can shine in life c) to shining in life d) so that he can shine in life
entries.correct_answer: d) so that he can shine in life
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'So that + subject + can/could + verb' is used to express purpose.

entries.question_text: রানী ছবি আঁকে।
entries.options_raw: a) Rani draw a picture. b) Rani drew a picture. c) Rani is drawing a picture. d) Rani draws a picture.
entries.explanation: Explanation: Habitual/present-simple action; third-person singular subject 'Rani' takes 'draws'.

entries.question_text: লোকটি হাসতে হাসতে আমার কাছে আসলো।

options.label: a
options.text: The man comes to me by laugh.

options.label: b
options.text: The man came to me by laugh.

options.label: c
options.text: The man came to me laughing.

options.label: d
options.text: The man coming to me laugh.

entries.options_raw: a) The man comes to me by laugh. b) The man came to me by laugh. c) The man came to me laughing. d) The man coming to me laugh.
entries.correct_answer: c) The man came to me laughing.
entries.explanation: Explanation: A participial phrase 'laughing' captures the simultaneous action 'হাসতে হাসতে'.

entries.question_text: সে কি গতকাল এসেছে?
entries.options_raw: a) Did he come yesterday? b) Did he came yesterday? c) Had he come yesterday? d) Has he come yesterday?
entries.explanation: Explanation: With a definite past-time indicator ('yesterday'), the past-simple interrogative form 'Did + subject + base verb' is used.

entries.question_text: অপমানের চেয়ে মৃত্যু শ্রেয়।
entries.options_raw: a) Death is better than insult. b) Death is preferable to dishonour. c) Dishonour is preferable than death. d) Death is acceptable than dishonour.
entries.correct_answer: b) Death is preferable to dishonour.
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Preferable' is followed by 'to' (never 'than'). The idiomatic English rendering is 'Death is preferable to dishonour.'

entries.question_text: বাংলাদেশ একটি নদীবহুল দেশ।

options.label: b
options.text: Bangladesh is a country of river.

entries.options_raw: a) Bangladesh is a riverine country. b) Bangladesh is a country of river. c) Bangladesh is surrounded by river. d) Bangladesh is situated by river.
entries.correct_answer: a) Bangladesh is a riverine country.
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Riverine' (adj.) = related to or abounding in rivers — the standard adjective for a country like Bangladesh with many rivers.

entries.question_text: আমার যদি পাখির মতো ডানা থাকত!

options.label: a
options.text: If I would have the wings of a bird!

options.label: b
options.text: Had I the wings of a bird!

options.label: c
options.text: I wish that I would have the wings of a bird!

options.label: d
options.text: If I could fly like a bird!

entries.options_raw: a) If I would have the wings of a bird! b) Had I the wings of a bird! c) I wish that I would have the wings of a bird! d) If I could fly like a bird!
entries.correct_answer: b) Had I the wings of a bird!
entries.explanation: Explanation: The inverted optative 'Had I…' expresses an unreal wish — the traditional literary rendering.

entries.question_text: মুষলধারে বৃষ্টি হচ্ছে।

options.label: c
options.text: It is raining cats and dogs.

entries.options_raw: a) It is raining heavily. b) It rains continuously. c) It is raining cats and dogs. d) It has been raining seriously.
entries.correct_answer: c) It is raining cats and dogs.
entries.explanation: Explanation: The idiomatic English equivalent of 'মুষলধারে বৃষ্টি' is 'raining cats and dogs' — a downpour.

entries.question_text: সে সাঁতার কাটতে জানে না।

options.label: a
options.text: He does not know how to swim.

options.label: b
options.text: He does not know to swim.

options.label: c
options.text: He donot knows how to swim.

entries.options_raw: a) He does not know how to swim. b) He does not know to swim. c) He donot knows how to swim. d) He cannot know to swim
entries.correct_answer: a) He does not know how to swim.
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Know how + to + verb' is the standard idiomatic pattern for expressing skill/ability.

entries.question_text: Prevention is better than —
entries.options_raw: a) nothing b) healing c) cure d) remedy
entries.explanation: Explanation: The classic English proverb 'Prevention is better than cure' — it is better to prevent a problem than to fix it afterwards.

entries.question_text: Knowledge is —
entries.options_raw: a) strength b) power c) gravity d) comfort
entries.explanation: Explanation: Francis Bacon's famous aphorism 'Knowledge is power' — knowledge gives one the ability to influence and control.

entries.question_text: What is lotted cannot be ________
entries.options_raw: a) blotted b) broken c) endured d) updated
entries.explanation: Explanation: The proverb 'What is lotted cannot be blotted' means whatever fate has decreed cannot be erased.

entries.question_text: সে ইংরেজিতে ভালো।
entries.options_raw: a) He is well in English. b) He is expert in English. c) He is good at English. d) He is better in English
entries.correct_answer: c) He is good at English.
entries.explanation: Explanation: The correct collocation is 'good at + subject/skill' — 'good at English/maths/singing'.

entries.question_text: জীবন পুষ্পশয্যা নয়।

options.label: a
options.text: The life is not bed of roses.

options.label: b
options.text: A life is not bed of roses.

options.label: c
options.text: Life is not bed of roses.

options.label: d
options.text: Life is not a bed of roses.

entries.options_raw: a) The life is not bed of roses. b) A life is not bed of roses. c) Life is not bed of roses. d) Life is not a bed of roses.
entries.correct_answer: d) Life is not a bed of roses.
entries.explanation: Explanation: The idiomatic English is 'a bed of roses' with the indefinite article 'a'; 'life' as a general concept takes no article.

entries.question_text: ইংরেজি শেখা সহজ।

options.label: b
options.text: The English is easy to learn.

options.label: c
options.text: It is easy to learning English.

options.label: d
options.text: It is easy to learn English.

entries.options_raw: a) English is easy for learning. b) The English is easy to learn. c) It is easy to learning English. d) It is easy to learn English.
entries.correct_answer: d) It is easy to learn English.
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'It is + adjective + to + base verb' is the standard extraposed subject structure.

entries.question_text: The journey was pleasant. Here 'pleasant' is ______
entries.options_raw: a) noun b) pronoun c) adjective d) adverb
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Pleasant' describes the noun 'journey' (as a predicate adjective after 'was') — hence it functions as an adjective.

entries.question_text: Lovely comes here regularly. Here 'Lovely' is ______
entries.options_raw: a) noun b) pronoun c) adjective d) adverb
entries.explanation: Explanation: Here 'Lovely' is used as the subject (a person's name), so it functions as a proper noun.

entries.question_text: The noun form of 'lose' is —
entries.options_raw: a) losing b) loss c) lost d) loose
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Lose' (verb) → 'loss' (noun). 'Losing' is gerund/present participle; 'lost' is the past/past participle.

entries.question_text: Honey is (taste) _______ sweet.
entries.options_raw: a) taste b) tasting c) tasted d) being tasted
entries.explanation: Explanation: Certain verbs of perception ('taste, smell, feel') combine with an adjective in the passive-participle form to describe a quality — 'is tasted sweet' functions here as 'tastes sweet' (NTRCA-approved form).

entries.question_text: It is our duty to (obey) _________ our parents.
entries.options_raw: a) obey b) obeying c) obeyed d) be obeyed
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'To + base verb' — the infinitive completes 'It is our duty to obey…'.

entries.question_text: Charity (to begin) — at home.
entries.options_raw: a) is beginning b) began c) begins d) has begun
entries.explanation: Explanation: The universal-truth/proverb form takes the simple present — 'Charity begins at home.'

entries.question_text: Something is better than ______
entries.options_raw: a) everything b) nothing c) anything d) all
entries.explanation: Explanation: The proverb 'Something is better than nothing' — having a little is better than having none.

entries.question_text: Many men, many _______
entries.options_raw: a) faces b) lives c) minds d) thoughts
entries.explanation: Explanation: The proverb 'Many men, many minds' — different people have different opinions/views.

entries.question_text: Out of sight, out of ________
entries.options_raw: a) life b) might c) mind d) right
entries.explanation: Explanation: The proverb 'Out of sight, out of mind' — people/things not seen tend to be forgotten.

entries.question_text: Only the moon was visible. (Negative)

options.label: c
options.text: Nothing but the moon was visible.

options.label: d
options.text: None but the moon was visible

entries.options_raw: a) The moon was not visible. b) The moon was not invisible. c) Nothing but the moon was visible. d) None but the moon was visible
entries.correct_answer: c) Nothing but the moon was visible.
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Only + non-personal noun' becomes 'Nothing but' in the negative form; 'Only + person' becomes 'None but'.

entries.question_text: Dhaka is one of the biggest cities in Bangladesh. (Positive)

options.label: a
options.text: No other cities in Bangladesh are as big as Dhaka.

options.label: b
options.text: Very few cities in Bangladesh are as big as Dhaka.

options.label: c
options.text: Very few cities in Bangladesh is as big as Dhaka.

options.label: d
options.text: Some cities in Bangladesh is as big as Dhaka.

entries.options_raw: a) No other cities in Bangladesh are as big as Dhaka. b) Very few cities in Bangladesh are as big as Dhaka. c) Very few cities in Bangladesh is as big as Dhaka. d) Some cities in Bangladesh is as big as Dhaka.
entries.correct_answer: b) Very few cities in Bangladesh are as big as Dhaka.
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'One of the + superlative' converts to 'Very few + noun + are as + positive-degree adjective + as + subject' in the positive.

entries.question_text: Never tell a lie. (Passive)

options.label: b
options.text: A lie is never be told.

options.label: c
options.text: Let a lie never be told.

options.label: d
options.text: Let not a lie be told ever.

entries.options_raw: a) A lie is never told. b) A lie is never be told. c) Let a lie never be told. d) Let not a lie be told ever.
entries.correct_answer: c) Let a lie never be told.
entries.explanation: Explanation: Negative imperative → passive using 'Let + object + never/not + be + past participle'.

entries.question_text: I have no pen that I can lend you. (Simple)

options.label: a
options.text: Having no pen, I can lend you.

options.label: b
options.text: Without any pen, I can lend you.

options.label: c
options.text: I have no pen to lend you.

options.label: d
options.text: I have not enough pen to lend

entries.options_raw: a) Having no pen, I can lend you. b) Without any pen, I can lend you. c) I have no pen to lend you. d) I have not enough pen to lend
entries.correct_answer: c) I have no pen to lend you.
entries.explanation: Explanation: The complex clause 'that I can lend you' becomes a simple infinitive 'to lend you'.

entries.question_text: The synonym of the word 'increase' is ______
entries.options_raw: a) augment b) decrease c) quick d) lessen
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Augment' = to make greater/increase. 'Decrease' and 'lessen' are antonyms.

entries.question_text: The antonym of the word 'alien' is __________
entries.options_raw: a) new comer b) native c) adverse d) foreigner
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Alien' = foreign/outsider; opposite is 'native' (belonging to a place by birth).

entries.question_text: The word 'usual' is the synonym of ________
entries.options_raw: a) normal b) certain c) unusual d) strange
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Usual' = habitual/customary/normal. 'Unusual' and 'strange' are antonyms.

entries.question_text: He is proud of his aristocracy. Here 'aristocracy' means ______
entries.options_raw: a) bad blood b) blue blood c) good blood d) cold blood
entries.explanation: Explanation: The idiom 'blue blood' = noble/aristocratic descent — 'aristocracy' matches this idiomatic sense.

entries.question_text: The man did the work as my direction. Here 'as' indicates the idiom —
entries.options_raw: a) as regards b) by all means c) according to d) at random
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'As' here functions to mean 'in accordance with' → the idiomatic equivalent is 'according to'.

entries.question_text: Smoking tells upon our body. Here 'tell upon' means ______
entries.options_raw: a) benefits b) harms c) indicates d) strengthens
entries.explanation: Explanation: The phrasal verb 'tell upon' = to have a bad effect on / to harm. So smoking 'tells upon' (harms) the body.

entries.question_text: Which one is the correct passive form of the sentence 'Your conduct pleased me'?

options.label: a
options.text: I am pleased of your conduct

options.label: b
options.text: I was pleased with your conduct

options.label: c
options.text: I was pleased by your conduct

options.label: d
options.text: I was pleased at your conduct

entries.options_raw: a) I am pleased of your conduct b) I was pleased with your conduct c) I was pleased by your conduct d) I was pleased at your conduct
entries.correct_answer: d) I was pleased at your conduct
entries.explanation: Explanation: The verb 'please' in the passive is followed by 'at' when referring to a cause/action (be pleased at something). NTRCA's answer-key marks (d) as correct.

entries.question_text: Choose the verb form of 'friend'.
entries.options_raw: a) friendship b) friended c) befriend d) enfriend
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Befriend' = to act as a friend to somebody. 'Friendship' = noun, 'enfriend' is not a standard word.

entries.question_text: 'তার জন্য জায়গা করে দাও' — এর শুদ্ধ ইংরেজি —
entries.options_raw: a) Make place for him b) Manage place for him c) Make accommodation for him d) Make room for him
entries.explanation: Explanation: The idiomatic English is 'make room for someone' (create space). 'Make place' is not idiomatic.

entries.question_text: What is the synonym of 'reveal'?
entries.options_raw: a) disclose b) conceal c) proclaim d) pacify
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Reveal' = to make known / disclose. 'Conceal' is the antonym; 'proclaim' means to announce publicly (a broader sense).

entries.question_text: Fill in the blank with appropriate preposition: I am pleased ____ hear about your promotion.
entries.options_raw: a) by b) to c) with d) for
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Pleased to + verb' — the infinitive form follows adjectives of emotion. 'Pleased to hear/see/meet' is standard.

entries.question_text: 'Swan song' means —
entries.options_raw: a) First work b) Last work c) Middle work d) Early work
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Swan song' is an idiom for the final performance or work of a person before their retirement or death — derived from the myth that swans sing beautifully just before dying.

entries.question_text: Sinners will suffer —
entries.options_raw: a) in fine b) in the long run c) in no time d) in the court
entries.explanation: Explanation: The idiom 'in the long run' = eventually, in the end. Sinners will eventually face consequences.

entries.question_text: 'All men must die' — Negative form of this sentence is —

options.label: b
options.text: None but all men will die

options.label: c
options.text: Nothing but all men must die

entries.options_raw: a) No men will never die b) None but all men will die c) Nothing but all men must die d) None can avoid death
entries.explanation: Explanation: The affirmative universal 'All must die' is rendered negatively as 'None can avoid death' — preserving the meaning of universality.

entries.question_text: I would rather die ________
entries.options_raw: a) to beg b) than beg c) than begging d) than would have begged
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Would rather + base verb + than + base verb' is the standard preference structure. 'I would rather die than beg.'

entries.question_text: Had I been rich, I ______.
entries.options_raw: a) would have helped the poor b) will help the poor c) had helped the poor d) than would have begged
entries.correct_answer: a) would have helped the poor
entries.explanation: Explanation: Inverted third-conditional structure: 'Had I been…' = 'If I had been…', main clause requires 'would/could/might have + past participle'.

entries.question_text: Do not insist ______ his going there.
entries.options_raw: a) to b) on c) with d) in
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Insist on + noun/gerund' is the fixed preposition pattern for the verb 'insist'.

entries.question_text: What is the noun form of 'believe'?
entries.options_raw: a) believe b) belief c) believable d) believance
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Believe' (verb) → 'belief' (noun). 'Believable' = adjective; 'believance' is not a word.

entries.question_text: Select the right word to fill in the sentence 'He ran fast lest he ________ miss the train.'
entries.options_raw: a) can b) should c) could d) would
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Lest' is always followed by 'should + base verb' — the classical/formal rule of English grammar.

entries.question_text: Phonetics is concerned with —
entries.options_raw: a) Pronunciation b) Word building c) Sentence making d) Passage
entries.explanation: Explanation: Phonetics is the scientific study of speech sounds — how they are produced, transmitted, and perceived, i.e., pronunciation.

entries.question_text: He advised me _______ smoking.
entries.options_raw: a) give up b) to stop c) to give up d) from giving up
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Advise + object + to + base verb' is the standard pattern. 'He advised me to give up smoking.'

entries.question_text: Would you mind (to take) simply a cup of coffee? The correct verb form would be —
entries.options_raw: a) to take b) taken c) taking d) for taking
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Mind' is always followed by a gerund (-ing form): 'Would you mind taking…'.

entries.question_text: The passive form of the sentence 'Do it as I say' is —

options.label: a
options.text: Let it be done as is said by me

options.label: b
options.text: Let it be done as I say

options.label: c
options.text: It should be done as I say

options.label: d
options.text: Be it done as it is said

entries.options_raw: a) Let it be done as is said by me b) Let it be done as I say c) It should be done as I say d) Be it done as it is said
entries.correct_answer: b) Let it be done as I say
entries.explanation: Explanation: Imperative 'Do it' → passive 'Let it be done'. The dependent clause 'as I say' stays unchanged.

entries.question_text: 'Blue blood' means —
entries.options_raw: a) aristocratic birth b) scoundrel c) fresh blood d) blood of king
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Blue blood' is an idiom meaning aristocratic descent / noble birth — from an old belief that noble families had visible blue veins because of fair skin.

entries.question_text: I look forward _______ you.
entries.options_raw: a) to see b) meeting c) to hearing from d) to meet
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Look forward to + gerund' is the fixed pattern. 'To hearing from you' correctly fits the phrase structure.

entries.question_text: We worked hard so that we ________ succeed.
entries.options_raw: a) can b) could c) may d) should
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'So that' clause takes 'could/might' when the main clause is in past tense. 'We worked (past) → we could succeed.'

entries.question_text: _______ water of this pond is clear. Use article.
entries.options_raw: a) The b) a c) no article d) an
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Water of this pond' refers to a specific quantity of water — the definite article 'the' is used before an uncountable noun modified by 'of'.

entries.question_text: Which one is a compound noun?
entries.options_raw: a) Headmaster b) Information c) Friday d) Examination
entries.explanation: Explanation: A compound noun is formed from two or more words. 'Headmaster' = head + master. 'Information' & 'examination' are derived nouns; 'Friday' is a proper noun.

entries.question_text: The man was ________ murder.
entries.options_raw: a) hung for b) hanged for c) hanged d) hung to
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Hang' has two past forms — 'hung' (for objects) and 'hanged' (for executing a person). 'Hanged for + crime' is the standard collocation.

entries.question_text: 'Head over heels in love' means —
entries.options_raw: a) loving somebody b) disliking somebody very much c) hating love strongly d) loving somebody very much
entries.explanation: Explanation: The idiom 'head over heels in love' = deeply, madly in love.

entries.question_text: Choose the correct sentence:

options.label: a
options.text: No sooner had I came than he went

options.label: b
options.text: No sooner I come than he went away

options.label: c
options.text: No sooner had I come when he went away

options.label: d
options.text: No sooner had I come than he went away

entries.options_raw: a) No sooner had I came than he went b) No sooner I come than he went away c) No sooner had I come when he went away d) No sooner had I come than he went away
entries.correct_answer: d) No sooner had I come than he went away
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'No sooner had + subject + past participle + than + past simple' — 'come' is the past participle of 'come'; 'than' (not 'when') is the correct correlative.

entries.question_text: No sooner ____ than the students stand up.

options.label: b
options.text: do the teacher enter the class

options.label: c
options.text: does the teacher enter the class

options.label: d
options.text: had the teacher entered the class

entries.options_raw: a) the teacher enter the class b) do the teacher enter the class c) does the teacher enter the class d) had the teacher entered the class
entries.correct_answer: d) had the teacher entered the class
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'No sooner… than…' takes the past-perfect inversion pattern: 'No sooner had + subject + past participle, than + past simple.'

entries.question_text: 1971 was the year _____
entries.options_raw: a) when Bangladesh is born b) when Bangladesh came to being c) when Bangladesh came into being d) when Bangladesh comes to being
entries.correct_answer: c) when Bangladesh came into being
entries.explanation: Explanation: The idiomatic English phrase is 'come into being' = to start to exist. Correct tense (past simple) for a 1971 event.

entries.question_text: Had I the wings of a bird ______.

options.label: b
options.text: I could fly in the sky

options.label: d
options.text: I would have flown in the sky

entries.options_raw: a) I flew in the sky b) I could fly in the sky c) I fly in the sky d) I would have flown in the sky
entries.correct_answer: b) I could fly in the sky
entries.explanation: Explanation: An inverted second-conditional structure ('Had I…' = 'If I had…') pairs with 'could + base verb' in the main clause.

entries.question_text: The man is too dishonest ______.
entries.options_raw: a) to tell a lie b) to take bribe c) to speak the truth d) to steal something
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Too + adjective + to + verb' carries a negative implication. 'Too dishonest to speak the truth' = so dishonest that he cannot speak the truth.

entries.question_text: It is many years since _____.
entries.options_raw: a) I meet you b) I met you c) I help you d) I have met you
entries.explanation: Explanation: The pattern 'It is + time + since + past simple' — the clause after 'since' takes the past simple.

entries.question_text: The old man walks slowly lest _____.
entries.options_raw: a) he falls b) he may fall c) he should fall d) he fell down
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Lest' (= for fear that) is always followed by 'should + base verb' in classical English usage.

entries.question_text: কতই না বিস্ময়কর মানুষের জীবন!

options.label: c
options.text: What an wonderful man's life is!

options.label: d
options.text: How wonderful a man's life is!

entries.options_raw: a) How strange man's life was! b) How strange man's life is! c) What an wonderful man's life is! d) How wonderful a man's life is!
entries.correct_answer: b) How strange man's life is!
entries.explanation: Explanation: Exclamatory 'How + adjective + subject + verb' — 'How strange man's life is!' matches the Bangla sense in the present tense.

entries.question_text: তার কোনো বন্ধু নেই বললেই চলে।
entries.options_raw: a) He has a few friends. b) He has no friends. c) He has few friends. d) He has the few friends.
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Few' (without article) carries a negative sense — 'hardly any', matching 'নেই বললেই চলে'. 'A few' is positive ('some').

entries.question_text: ভাই ভাই ঠাঁই ঠাঁই।
entries.options_raw: a) Brothers part. b) Brothers will part. c) Brothers will be part. d) Brothers have parted.
entries.explanation: Explanation: The Bangla proverb 'ভাই ভাই ঠাঁই ঠাঁই' means brothers ultimately separate — expressed in English as a general future truth 'Brothers will part.'

entries.question_text: শিশুটি কাঁদতে কাঁদতে আমার কাছে এল।

options.label: a
options.text: The child comes to me run.

options.label: b
options.text: The child came to me running.

options.label: c
options.text: The child came to me crying.

options.label: d
options.text: The child came to me to cry.

entries.options_raw: a) The child comes to me run. b) The child came to me running. c) The child came to me crying. d) The child came to me to cry.
entries.correct_answer: c) The child came to me crying.
entries.explanation: Explanation: A participial phrase 'crying' describes the simultaneous action — 'came… crying' matches the Bangla 'কাঁদতে কাঁদতে'.

entries.question_text: তুমি কি কখনও কক্সবাজার গিয়েছ?

options.label: a
options.text: Have you ever been to Cox's Bazar?

options.label: b
options.text: Did you ever go to Cox's Bazar?

options.label: c
options.text: Have you ever go to Cox's Bazar?

options.label: d
options.text: Have you gone to Cox's Bazar?

entries.options_raw: a) Have you ever been to Cox's Bazar? b) Did you ever go to Cox's Bazar? c) Have you ever go to Cox's Bazar? d) Have you gone to Cox's Bazar?
entries.correct_answer: a) Have you ever been to Cox's Bazar?
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Have + subject + ever + been to + place' is the standard present-perfect question for past experience of visiting a place.

entries.question_text: I wish I _______ child again.
entries.options_raw: a) be b) am c) was d) were
entries.explanation: Explanation: After 'I wish', the subjunctive form 'were' is used for all subjects to express an unreal/present wish.

entries.question_text: Two and two ____ four.
entries.options_raw: a) make b) makes c) made d) make/makes
entries.explanation: Explanation: In arithmetic statements, 'two and two' is treated as a single quantity, so it takes a singular verb — 'makes'.

entries.question_text: It is high time we ______ our food habits.
entries.options_raw: a) give up b) gave up c) changed d) changing
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'It is high time + subject + past simple' — subjunctive expressing that an action is overdue. Semantically 'changed' fits 'food habits' better than 'gave up'.

entries.question_text: The headmaster along with his colleagues ____ coming here today.
entries.options_raw: a) is b) are c) will d) was
entries.explanation: Explanation: When two subjects are joined by 'along with / together with / as well as', the verb agrees with the first subject ('The headmaster' — singular).

entries.question_text: It ______ since morning.
entries.options_raw: a) has rained b) has been raining c) is raining d) has rained/has been raining
entries.explanation: Explanation: Both present perfect ('has rained') and present perfect continuous ('has been raining') are grammatically acceptable with 'since morning' — hence (d) covers both correct forms.

entries.question_text: Birds fly _______ in the sky.
entries.options_raw: a) at a stretch b) at large c) all along d) at random
entries.explanation: Explanation: The idiom 'at large' here means 'freely, without restraint' — birds flying free in the sky.

entries.question_text: "Tooth and nail" means _______
entries.options_raw: a) get by heart b) go with heart c) tried hard d) get hard
entries.explanation: Explanation: The idiom 'tooth and nail' = with utmost effort and determination; 'fight tooth and nail' ≈ tried hard.

entries.question_text: 'Big bug' means ____ .
entries.options_raw: a) useful person b) important person c) unemployed person d) employed person
entries.explanation: Explanation: The idiom 'big bug' (also 'big shot / big wig') = a very important/influential person.

entries.question_text: The price of rice is increasing ____ .
entries.options_raw: a) by fits and starts b) by dint of c) by virtue of d) by leaps and bounds
entries.explanation: Explanation: The idiom 'by leaps and bounds' = very rapidly and by large amounts — fits the sense of rapidly rising prices.

entries.question_text: Della was too poor to buy a gift for Jim. (Negative)

options.label: a
options.text: Della was not too poor to buy a gift for Jim.

options.label: b
options.text: Della was so poor that he could not buy a gift for Jim.

options.label: c
options.text: Della was so poor that she could not buy a gift for Jim.

options.label: d
options.text: Della was so poor that she cannot buy a gift for Jim.

entries.options_raw: a) Della was not too poor to buy a gift for Jim. b) Della was so poor that he could not buy a gift for Jim. c) Della was so poor that she could not buy a gift for Jim. d) Della was so poor that she cannot buy a gift for Jim.
entries.correct_answer: c) Della was so poor that she could not buy a gift for Jim.
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Too + adjective + to + verb' → 'so + adjective + that + subject + could not + verb'; correct pronoun 'she' (Della is female).

entries.question_text: Nobody wishes to be unhappy. (Interrogative)

options.label: c
options.text: Who does not wish to be unhappy?

options.label: d
options.text: Does nobody wish to be happy?

entries.options_raw: a) Who wishes to be unhappy? b) Who wishes to be happy? c) Who does not wish to be unhappy? d) Does nobody wish to be happy?
entries.correct_answer: a) Who wishes to be unhappy?
entries.explanation: Explanation: A negative universal statement ('Nobody wishes X') → rhetorical question 'Who wishes X?' — expecting the answer 'nobody'.

entries.question_text: Unemployment is a state for a man having no work to earn money. (Complex)

options.label: a
options.text: Unemployment is a state when a man has no work to earn money

options.label: b
options.text: Unemployment is a state for a man who has no work to earn money

options.label: c
options.text: Unemployment is a state of a man who has no work.

options.label: d
options.text: Unemployment is the condition of a man who has no work

entries.options_raw: a) Unemployment is a state when a man has no work to earn money b) Unemployment is a state for a man who has no work to earn money c) Unemployment is a state of a man who has no work. d) Unemployment is the condition of a man who has no work
entries.correct_answer: b) Unemployment is a state for a man who has no work to earn money
entries.explanation: Explanation: The participial phrase 'having no work…' is expanded into a relative clause 'who has no work…' — creating a complex sentence.

entries.question_text: Noun of the word 'simple' is ______.
entries.options_raw: a) simply b) simplify c) simplicity d) simplication
entries.explanation: Explanation: Noun form of 'simple' = 'simplicity'. 'Simply' = adverb, 'simplify' = verb.

entries.question_text: Find out the correct synonym of 'hazard'.
entries.options_raw: a) Impartial b) Static c) Impolite d) Danger
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Hazard' = a source of danger or risk; closest synonym is 'danger'.

entries.question_text: The fruit is sweet ______ the taste.
entries.options_raw: a) by b) with c) for d) to
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Sweet by taste' — the preposition 'by' is used with adjectives to indicate the means/manner of description (e.g., good by nature, bitter by taste).

entries.question_text: Did he see anyone in the room? (Assertive)

options.label: a
options.text: He saw no one in the room.

options.label: b
options.text: He did not see someone in the room.

options.label: c
options.text: He saw anyone in the room.

options.label: d
options.text: He saw someone in the room.

entries.options_raw: a) He saw no one in the room. b) He did not see someone in the room. c) He saw anyone in the room. d) He saw someone in the room.
entries.correct_answer: a) He saw no one in the room.
entries.explanation: Explanation: The negative-rhetorical question 'Did he see anyone…?' implies a strong negative — assertively rendered as 'He saw no one in the room.'

entries.question_text: I have no money ______ hand.
entries.options_raw: a) in b) by c) at d) on
entries.explanation: Explanation: The fixed phrase 'in hand' means 'immediately available/at one's disposal'. 'Money in hand' = ready cash.

entries.question_text: It is health which is _____.
entries.options_raw: a) asset b) wealth c) valuable d) precious
entries.explanation: Explanation: The proverb 'Health is wealth' — completing the cleft sentence with 'wealth' preserves the well-known idiom.

entries.question_text: If we practised speaking English, we ________ speak better.
entries.options_raw: a) could b) could have c) can d) would have
entries.explanation: Explanation: Second-conditional structure: 'If + past simple, subject + would/could + base verb'. 'If we practised… we could speak better.'

entries.question_text: He and I ______ well.
entries.options_raw: a) am b) is c) are d) been
entries.explanation: Explanation: A compound subject ('He and I') is plural and takes the plural verb 'are'.

entries.question_text: এটা যেন বিনা মেঘে বজ্রপাত।

options.label: a
options.text: It is as if a thunder from the clouds.

options.label: b
options.text: It is a bolt from the blue.

options.label: d
options.text: It is bolts from the blues.

entries.options_raw: a) It is as if a thunder from the clouds. b) It is a bolt from the blue. c) It is a strong thunder. d) It is bolts from the blues.
entries.correct_answer: b) It is a bolt from the blue.
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'A bolt from the blue' is the idiomatic English equivalent of 'বিনা মেঘে বজ্রপাত' — a sudden, unexpected calamity.

entries.question_text: সে এক সপ্তাহ যাবৎ অসুস্থ।

options.label: a
options.text: He has been ill since a week.

options.label: b
options.text: He has been ill till a week.

options.label: c
options.text: He has been ill for a week.

options.label: d
options.text: He has been ill during a week.

entries.options_raw: a) He has been ill since a week. b) He has been ill till a week. c) He has been ill for a week. d) He has been ill during a week.
entries.correct_answer: c) He has been ill for a week.
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'For' is used with a duration/period (a week, five days), while 'since' is used with a specific point in time.

entries.question_text: দাঁড়াও, আমি এখনি আসছি।

options.label: c
options.text: Keep standing, I am coming now.

entries.options_raw: a) Stand, I come now. b) Wait, I am coming now. c) Keep standing, I am coming now. d) Stand here, I am coming.
entries.correct_answer: b) Wait, I am coming now.
entries.explanation: Explanation: The colloquial 'দাঁড়াও' here means 'wait', not literally 'stand'. Present continuous 'am coming' captures the immediate future action.

entries.question_text: জ্ঞানীরা বেশি কথা বলেন না।

options.label: a
options.text: The wises do not talk much.

options.label: b
options.text: The wise does not talk much.

options.label: c
options.text: The wise do not talk much.

options.label: d
options.text: The wise men does not talk much.

entries.options_raw: a) The wises do not talk much. b) The wise does not talk much. c) The wise do not talk much. d) The wise men does not talk much.
entries.correct_answer: c) The wise do not talk much.
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'The + adjective' (the wise, the rich, the poor) denotes a plural group and takes a plural verb — 'The wise do…'

entries.question_text: He came to Dhaka with a view to ______ a new place.
entries.options_raw: a) visit b) visiting c) watch d) look
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'With a view to' is always followed by the gerund (-ing form): 'with a view to visiting'.

entries.question_text: Some interesting facts about your past have just come to light. Here 'come to light' means —
entries.options_raw: a) go near to light b) to become known c) to realize d) to lit a light
entries.explanation: Explanation: The idiom 'come to light' = to be revealed / to become publicly known.

entries.question_text: The passive form of 'Don't do it' is —
entries.options_raw: a) Let not it be done. b) Let it be not done. c) Let it be done. d) Let it not be done.
entries.correct_answer: a) Let not it be done.
entries.explanation: Explanation: For a negative imperative, the traditional passive form used by NTRCA answer-key is 'Let not it be done.' (Some grammarians prefer 'Let it not be done', but option (a) was marked correct.)

entries.question_text: The synonym of the word 'scream' is —
entries.options_raw: a) yell b) sound c) cry d) loudly
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Scream' = to shout loudly, especially from pain or fear. 'Yell' is the closest synonym.

entries.question_text: I (help) you if I could.
entries.options_raw: a) I would help b) I would be helped c) I helped d) I would have helped

entries.explanation: Explanation: 'So…that…not' becomes 'too…to…' in a simple sentence.

entries.question_text: He is the best player. (Negative)

options.label: a

entries.correct_answer: b) No other player is as good as he.

entries.question_text: Read to learn. (Complex)

options.label: c

options.label: d

entries.question_text: Look before you leap. The word 'before' used in the sentence is —
entries.options_raw: a) preposition b) conjunction c) adverb d) noun
entries.explanation: Explanation: Here 'before' joins two clauses ('Look' and 'you leap'), so it functions as a subordinating conjunction.

entries.question_text: Please look above. Here 'above' is —
entries.options_raw: a) adjective b) adverb c) noun d) conjunction
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Above' modifies the verb 'look' (indicating direction), so it functions as an adverb.

entries.question_text: Grasp all, ______
entries.options_raw: a) lost all b) losing all c) loses all d) lose all
entries.explanation: Explanation: The proverb 'Grasp all, lose all' — those who try to seize everything end up losing everything. Parallel imperative form.

entries.question_text: Death is ____ to dishonour.
entries.options_raw: a) prefer b) preferrence c) preferable d) referring
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Preferable to' — an adjective meaning 'better than'. The blank needs an adjective after 'is'.

entries.question_text: It takes two ______ make a quarrel.
entries.options_raw: a) too b) for c) to d) in order to
entries.explanation: Explanation: The proverb 'It takes two to make a quarrel' — a quarrel needs the participation of both parties. Simple 'to'-infinitive.

entries.question_text: The synonym of the word 'call' is —
entries.options_raw: a) summon b) exile c) impede d) recollection
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Summon' means to officially call/order someone to come — closest synonym to 'call'.

entries.question_text: The antonym of the word 'liberty' is —
entries.options_raw: a) liberal b) bondage c) frugal d) diversity
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Liberty' = freedom; its opposite is 'bondage' = slavery/servitude.

entries.question_text: The judge acquitted him _____ the charge.
entries.options_raw: ক) from খ) of গ) on ঘ) in
entries.explanation: 'Acquit somebody of a charge' নির্দিষ্ট collocation — অভিযোগ থেকে অব্যাহতি দেওয়া।

entries.question_text: The noun form of "endure" is —
entries.options_raw: ক) endurance খ) endurement গ) endurence ঘ) endurable
entries.explanation: Endure (verb, সহ্য করা) → Endurance (noun, সহনশীলতা); Endurable (adj., সহনযোগ্য)।

entries.question_text: ____ mother rose in her.
entries.options_raw: ক) A খ) An গ) No article ঘ) The
entries.explanation: বিশেষ অর্থে/গুণে ('মাতৃসত্তা') noun-এর আগে 'the' বসে। 'The mother rose in her' — তার মধ্যে মাতৃত্ববোধ জাগ্রত হলো।

entries.question_text: He complied _____ her request.
entries.options_raw: ক) on খ) with গ) to ঘ) by
entries.explanation: 'Comply with' নির্দিষ্ট collocation — কারো অনুরোধ/নির্দেশ মেনে চলা।

entries.question_text: The adjective form of 'heart' is ____
entries.options_raw: ক) heartly খ) heartily গ) hearty ঘ) heartable
entries.explanation: Heart (noun) → Hearty (adj., আন্তরিক); Heartily (adv.); Hearten (verb)। 'Heartly' প্রকৃত শব্দ নয়।

entries.question_text: ____ honesty of Rahim is enviable.
entries.options_raw: ক) The খ) A গ) An ঘ) No article
entries.explanation: নির্দিষ্ট ব্যক্তির (Rahim-এর) সততা বোঝাতে 'the' বসে। Abstract noun 'honesty' নির্দিষ্ট প্রেক্ষাপটে 'the' গ্রহণ করে।

entries.question_text: Choose the correct sentence:

options.text: He lived here for five months.

entries.question_text: Check ____ beast in you.
entries.options_raw: ক) the খ) a গ) an ঘ) no article
entries.explanation: রূপক অর্থে ('পশুসত্তা') noun-এর আগে 'the' বসে — 'the beast in you' = তোমার ভেতরের পশুসত্তা।

entries.question_text: What is the plural number of 'spectrum'?
entries.options_raw: ক) Spectrums খ) Spectra গ) Species ঘ) Image
entries.explanation: ল্যাটিন-উৎস noun-এর plural: Spectrum → Spectra; Datum → Data; Medium → Media।

entries.question_text: "Null and void" means ___
entries.options_raw: ক) invalid খ) valid গ) lawful ঘ) incorrect
entries.explanation: 'Null and void' আইনি idiom — সম্পূর্ণ অকার্যকর/বাতিল (having no legal force)।

entries.question_text: 'Apple of one's eye' means —
entries.options_raw: ক) apple like eye খ) big eye গ) apple coloured eye ঘ) extremely favourite
entries.explanation: 'Apple of one's eye' idiom — অত্যন্ত প্রিয়/আদরের ব্যক্তি বা বস্তু। যেমন: The child is the apple of his mother's eye.

entries.question_text: The correct sentence is —

options.text: Two third of it is fine

options.label: গ
options.text: Two thirds of it are fine

entries.options_raw: ক) Two thirds of it is fine খ) Two third of it is fine গ) Two thirds of it are fine ঘ) Two third is fine
entries.correct_answer: ক) Two thirds of it is fine
entries.explanation: 'Two-thirds' — সঠিক ভগ্নাংশ (multiple, তাই plural 's'); of-এর পরের noun ('it', uncountable) singular হওয়ায় verb 'is'।

entries.question_text: He acted ___ strong opposition.
entries.options_raw: ক) in teeth খ) in teeth of গ) in the teeth of ঘ) by the teeth of
entries.explanation: 'In the teeth of' idiom — সরাসরি বিরোধিতা/বিরুদ্ধতার মুখেও (in direct opposition to)। সঠিক: He acted in the teeth of strong opposition.

entries.question_text: The passive form of the sentence "Enter the house by this gate" is —

options.label: ক

options.label: খ
options.text: You should enter the house by this gate.

options.label: গ
options.text: Let the house be entered by this gate.

options.label: ঘ
options.text: Let the house be entered by you by this gate.

entries.options_raw: ক) You are requested to enter the house by this gate. খ) You should enter the house by this gate. গ) Let the house be entered by this gate. ঘ) Let the house be entered by you by this gate.
entries.correct_answer: ক) You are requested to enter the house by this gate.
entries.explanation: NTRCA-স্বীকৃত রূপান্তর — imperative-এর passive-এ 'You are requested to + V' গঠন ব্যবহৃত হয় সৌজন্যসূচক অনুরোধে।

entries.question_text: The passive form of "Who has broken the glass"? is —

options.label: ক
options.text: By who have the glass been broken?

options.label: খ

options.text: By whom have the glass been broken?

options.label: ঘ
options.text: Whom has the glass been broken?

entries.options_raw: ক) By who have the glass been broken? খ) By whom has the glass been broken? গ) By whom have the glass been broken? ঘ) Whom has the glass been broken?
entries.correct_answer: খ) By whom has the glass been broken?
entries.explanation: Interrogative 'Who' → passive-এ 'By whom + auxiliary + subject + V3?' গঠন। Object 'the glass' (singular) → 'has been broken'।

entries.question_text: It is high time he (change) his bad habits.
entries.options_raw: ক) changing খ) has changed গ) changed ঘ) has been changing
entries.explanation: 'It is high time' এর পরে subject + past simple (subjunctive) বসে; বর্তমান কালীন হলেও verb past form নেয়।

entries.question_text: The children were entrusted ___ the care of their uncle.
entries.options_raw: ক) with খ) for গ) to ঘ) at
entries.explanation: 'Entrust something/somebody to somebody' — কাউকে কারো তত্ত্বাবধানে ন্যস্ত করা। সঠিক: were entrusted to the care of their uncle.

entries.question_text: The antonym of 'belligerent' is ___
entries.options_raw: ক) bellicose খ) pugnacious গ) peaceful ঘ) silent
entries.explanation: 'Belligerent' (adj.) — যুদ্ধপ্রবণ/আক্রমণাত্মক; বিপরীত 'peaceful' — শান্তিপ্রিয়। Bellicose, pugnacious — সমার্থক।

entries.question_text: He suffered from the ____ that he was another Napoleon.
entries.options_raw: ক) imagination খ) illusion গ) diffusion ঘ) allusion
entries.explanation: 'Illusion' — মিথ্যা ধারণা/বিভ্রম। বাক্যের অর্থ — সে নেপোলিয়নের মতো এই মিথ্যা বিভ্রমে ভুগত। Allusion = ইঙ্গিত; diffusion = ছড়িয়ে পড়া।

entries.question_text: Identify the correct spelling.
entries.options_raw: ক) acquaintance খ) acquaintence গ) acquantence ঘ) acquintence
entries.explanation: শুদ্ধ বানান 'acquaintance' (পরিচিতি/পরিচয়); '-ance' প্রত্যয়যুক্ত।

entries.question_text: It ____ since morning.
entries.options_raw: ক) rains খ) has rained গ) has been raining ঘ) will be raining
entries.explanation: 'Since morning' চলমান কাজ → present perfect continuous ('has been raining')।

entries.question_text: While he ____ in the garden, a snake bit him.
entries.options_raw: ক) walked খ) walks গ) is walking ঘ) was walking
entries.explanation: 'While' যুক্ত ও অপর অংশ past simple ('bit') হলে while-clause-এ past continuous ('was walking')।

entries.question_text: If I had a typewriter, ___
entries.options_raw: ক) I will type myself খ) I would have typed myself গ) I would type myself ঘ) I might have typed myself
entries.explanation: Second conditional (unreal present) — If + past simple ('had'), main clause 'would + V' ('would type')।

entries.question_text: You had better ____ him at once.
entries.options_raw: ক) to ring খ) ring গ) ringing ঘ) rung
entries.explanation: 'Had better' + bare infinitive (without 'to')। সঠিক: You had better ring him at once.

entries.question_text: "A child liked only sweets" — Negative form of this sentence is ____

entries.explanation: 'Only + noun' যুক্ত assertive → Negative-এ 'nothing but + noun' গঠন। সঠিক: A child likes nothing but sweets.

entries.question_text: তিনি কদাচিৎ মিথ্যা কথা বলেন।

entries.question_text: ভুল করা মানুষের স্বভাব।
entries.options_raw: ক) To err is human খ) To err is a human গ) To err is human ঘ) To erro human
entries.explanation: NTRCA কর্তৃপক্ষ প্রশ্নটি বাতিল করেছে। (অপশন 'ক' ও 'গ' হুবহু একই — 'To err is human'; দুটি একই সঠিক উত্তর থাকায় প্রশ্নটি বাতিল।)

entries.question_text: নাই মামার চেয়ে কানা মামা ভাল।

options.text: Some uncles are better than no uncle

entries.explanation: প্রবাদটির ইংরেজি সংস্করণ 'Something is better than nothing' — কিছু না থাকার চেয়ে সামান্য কিছু ভালো।

entries.question_text: লোকটির মরমর অবস্থা।

entries.explanation: 'About to + V' — অতি নিকট ভবিষ্যতের কাজ প্রকাশ করে; 'মরমর অবস্থা' = মৃত্যুর ঠিক আগের অবস্থা।

entries.question_text: আমি তাকে দিয়ে কাজটি করালাম।

entries.correct_answer: ক) I made him do the work
entries.explanation: Causative 'make' + object + bare infinitive। সঠিক: I made him do the work.

entries.correct_answer: গ) Belal is better than any other boy in the class
entries.explanation: Superlative → Comparative: 'better than any other + singular noun'। 'Any other boy' — সঠিক গঠন।

entries.question_text: Everybody hates a liar. (Interrogative)

options.text: Who does not hate a liar?

entries.correct_answer: ঘ) Who does not hate a liar?
entries.explanation: 'Everybody' universal affirmative → Interrogative-এ 'Who does not + bare infinitive?' গঠন। সঠিক: Who does not hate a liar?

entries.question_text: He is poor but he is honest. (Complex)

options.label: ক

options.label: গ
options.text: As he is poor, he is honest

options.text: Since he is poor, he is honest

entries.correct_answer: ক) Though he is poor, he is honest
entries.explanation: 'But' compound conjunction → Complex-এ 'Though/Although' subordinating conjunction ব্যবহৃত হয়। সঠিক: Though he is poor, he is honest.

entries.question_text: He is so weak that he cannot walk. (Simple)

entries.correct_answer: গ) He is too weak to walk
entries.explanation: 'So ... that ... cannot ...' → Simple-এ 'too ... to ...' গঠনে রূপান্তরিত হয়।

entries.question_text: 'Milk and Water' means —
entries.options_raw: ক) brave খ) timid গ) daring ঘ) courageous
entries.explanation: 'Milk and Water' idiom — দুর্বল/ভীরু/মিনমিনে চরিত্র (timid/weak-charactered)। যেমন: a milk-and-water response.

entries.question_text: Politicians often use students as ____.
entries.options_raw: ক) cat's paw খ) timid গ) daring ঘ) kith and kin
entries.explanation: 'Cat's paw' idiom — ঘুঁটি/অন্যের হাতের পুতুল (someone used by another as a tool)। রাজনৈতিক প্রেক্ষাপটে খুব উপযুক্ত অভিব্যক্তি।

entries.question_text: Sher-e Bangla was a —
entries.options_raw: ক) man of sorrow খ) man of justice গ) man of mark ঘ) out and out
entries.explanation: 'Man of mark' idiom — উল্লেখযোগ্য/বিশিষ্ট ব্যক্তি (a person of distinction)। শের-এ-বাংলা এ. কে. ফজলুল হক ছিলেন বাংলার একজন প্রখ্যাত রাজনৈতিক নেতা।

entries.question_text: He is _______ a rogue.
entries.options_raw: ক) above all খ) after all গ) one and every ঘ) out and out
entries.explanation: 'Out and out' idiom — পুরোপুরি/সম্পূর্ণভাবে (completely/thoroughly)। বাক্যের অর্থ — সে পুরোপুরি একটি বদমাশ।

entries.question_text: I saw the beggar _____on the floor.
entries.options_raw: ক) laid খ) lying গ) lay ঘ) lie
entries.explanation: Sensory verb (see) + object + verb-ing — চলমান কাজ দেখা বোঝায়। 'Lie' (শুয়ে থাকা)-এর present participle 'lying'।

entries.question_text: I went to the library with a view to ____ knowledge.
entries.options_raw: ক) gain খ) gaining গ) gained ঘ) be gained
entries.explanation: 'With a view to' এর পরে সবসময় gerund (verb-ing) বসে। সঠিক: with a view to gaining knowledge.

entries.question_text: The poor _____ much in winter.
entries.options_raw: ক) suffer খ) suffers গ) suffering ঘ) suffered
entries.explanation: 'The + adjective' (the poor, the rich, the sick) plural noun হিসেবে কাজ করে, plural verb নেয়। সঠিক: The poor suffer much in winter.

entries.question_text: Walk fast lest you (miss) the train.
entries.options_raw: ক) would miss খ) missed গ) should miss ঘ) will miss
entries.explanation: 'Lest' conjunction-এর পরে subject + should + bare infinitive। সঠিক: lest you should miss.

entries.question_text: The patient (die) before the doctor came.
entries.options_raw: ক) died খ) had died গ) have died ঘ) would died
entries.explanation: 'Before'-এর পর past simple ('came') হলে earlier action past perfect ('had died')।

entries.question_text: I (to suffer) from fever for three days.
entries.options_raw: ক) have suffered খ) am suffering গ) suffered ঘ) have been suffering
entries.explanation: 'For three days' — চলমান দীর্ঘস্থায়ী কাজ; present perfect continuous ('have been suffering') সবচেয়ে উপযুক্ত।

entries.question_text: "তাকে তিরস্কার করা হয়েছিল" এর শুদ্ধ ইংরেজি —

entries.explanation: 'Bring to book' idiom — কাউকে তিরস্কার/জবাবদিহি করানো, শাস্তির আওতায় আনা। NTRCA-স্বীকৃত অনুবাদ এটাই।

entries.question_text: We helped him __ the work.

entries.question_text: He fought ____ to defeat the enemy.
entries.options_raw: ক) tooth and nail খ) set out গ) to and fro ঘ) to the quick
entries.explanation: 'Fight tooth and nail' idiom — প্রাণপণ/সর্বশক্তি দিয়ে লড়াই করা। শত্রুকে পরাজিত করতে যথাসাধ্য চেষ্টার প্রেক্ষাপটে যথার্থ।

entries.question_text: When you make a promise, you must not go ___ on it.
entries.options_raw: ক) by খ) around গ) back ঘ) along

entries.question_text: What type of man is quite the opposite type of 'Supercilious'?

entries.options_raw: ক) which খ) what গ) whatever ঘ) whatsoever
entries.explanation: 'It is ... which/that ...' cleft sentence — জোর দিয়ে বলার গঠন। Non-restrictive relative pronoun 'which' এখানে যথার্থ।

entries.question_text: The boy is _______ answer the question.
entries.options_raw: ক) to dull too খ) too dull to গ) to dull to ঘ) to very dull
entries.explanation: 'Too + adjective + to + verb' গঠন — এতটাই ... যে ... করতে পারে না। সঠিক: too dull to answer the question.

entries.explanation: 'In case' এর পর সাধারণত simple present বা past subjunctive; principal clause past tense ('carried') হলে subordinate clause-এ past tense 'rained'।

options.label: ক

options.label: খ
options.text: The girl prefers milk to tea

options.label: গ
options.text: The girl prefers milk than tea

options.label: ঘ
options.text: The girl prefers tea to milk

entries.correct_answer: খ) The girl prefers milk to tea

entries.correct_answer: খ) It has been raining cats and dogs since morning
entries.explanation: চলমান কাজ ('সকাল থেকে') → present perfect continuous ('has been raining')। নির্দিষ্ট সময়-বিন্দু ('morning') → 'since'। 'Rain cats and dogs' idiom = মুষলধারে বৃষ্টি।

entries.explanation: অতীতে পূর্বনির্ধারিত/কথা-দেওয়া কাজ বোঝাতে 'was/were + to + infinitive' গঠন ব্যবহৃত হয়। সঠিক: I was to go to Manikganj.

entries.question_text: Would that I ______ to college.
entries.options_raw: ক) can go খ) shall go গ) could go ঘ) might have gone
entries.explanation: 'Would that' optative gesture — কামনা/আশা প্রকাশ করে; পরে 'could + V' বসে। সঠিক: Would that I could go to college.

entries.question_text: I wish I _______ a sweet song.
entries.options_raw: ক) sang খ) shall sing গ) can sing ঘ) will sing
entries.explanation: 'I wish' এর পর অবাস্তব বর্তমান বা অতীত ইচ্ছা প্রকাশে subjunctive past ('sang') ব্যবহৃত হয়।

entries.question_text: He spoke as though he _______ everything.
entries.options_raw: ক) knew খ) has known গ) had known ঘ) knows
entries.explanation: Principal clause past ('spoke') হলে 'as though'-এর পরে past perfect ('had known') বসে — যেন তিনি আগেই সব জানতেন।

entries.question_text: The colour of her eyes _____ blue.
entries.options_raw: ক) are খ) is গ) were ঘ) none of the above
entries.explanation: Main subject 'The colour' (singular) → verb 'is'। 'Of her eyes' modifier — verb-এর সংখ্যা প্রভাবিত করে না।

entries.question_text: 'Ten to one' means _______
entries.options_raw: ক) very uncertain খ) very likely গ) almost impossible ঘ) not possible at all
entries.explanation: 'Ten to one' idiom — খুবই সম্ভাব্য (very likely/almost certain)। বাজি রাখার ভাষা থেকে উদ্ভূত।

entries.question_text: He insisted _______ there.
entries.options_raw: ক) over going খ) on my going গ) to go ঘ) is to go
entries.explanation: 'Insist on + possessive + verb-ing' — নির্দিষ্ট গঠন। সঠিক: He insisted on my going there.

entries.correct_answer: খ) Jim and Della were not less wise than the Magi

entries.question_text: Find out the correct synonym of 'occupy'
entries.options_raw: ক) grab খ) gain গ) receive ঘ) reserve
entries.explanation: 'Occupy' মানে দখল করা; সবচেয়ে কাছাকাছি সমার্থক 'grab' (দ্রুত ধরে নেওয়া/দখল)।

entries.question_text: Find out the correct synonym of 'defence'
entries.options_raw: ক) assault খ) resistance গ) attack ঘ) raid
entries.explanation: 'Defence' মানে আত্মরক্ষা/প্রতিরোধ; সমার্থক 'resistance'। Assault, attack, raid — বিপরীত (আক্রমণ)।

entries.question_text: Find out the antonym of 'assist'.
entries.options_raw: ক) hinder খ) aid গ) support ঘ) co-operate
entries.explanation: 'Assist' = সাহায্য করা; বিপরীত 'hinder' — বাধা দেওয়া। Aid, support, co-operate সমার্থক।

entries.question_text: What is the noun form of the word 'successful'?

entries.question_text: Verb of the word 'apology' is _______
entries.options_raw: ক) apological খ) apologise গ) apologify ঘ) enapology
entries.explanation: Apology (noun) → Apologise/Apologize (verb, ক্ষমাপ্রার্থনা করা)। 'Apological' প্রকৃত শব্দ নয়।

entries.question_text: Educating all people _____ a mammoth task.
entries.options_raw: ক) are খ) is গ) be ঘ) have
entries.explanation: Gerund phrase 'Educating all people' singular subject হিসেবে কাজ করছে, তাই singular verb 'is'। 'Mammoth' মানে বিশাল/বৃহৎ।

entries.question_text: Today the world is passing through _______ juncture.

entries.question_text: The old man cannot help ______ a cup of tea.
entries.options_raw: ক) take খ) drink গ) to drink ঘ) having
entries.explanation: 'Cannot help + verb-ing' নির্দিষ্ট গঠন — না করে পারা যায় না। 'Have a cup of tea' idiom — চা পান করা। তাই 'having' সঠিক।

entries.question_text: There is _______ milk in the bottle.

entries.explanation: 'Milk' uncountable noun; পরিমাণ কম বোঝাতে 'little/very little' ব্যবহৃত হয়। Few/many countable noun-এর জন্য।

entries.explanation: 'Beggars description' idiom — বর্ণনার অতীত (indescribable)। Subject 'suffering' (singular) → verb 'beggars' (s-সহ)।

entries.question_text: I wish I had seen you before. (Exclamatory)
entries.options_raw: ক) Wow! I seen you before. খ) Had I seen you before! গ) Oh! I seen you before. ঘ) If I seen you before
entries.correct_answer: খ) Had I seen you before!
entries.explanation: 'I wish I had + V3' → Exclamatory 'Had I + V3 ...!' গঠন হয় — অতীতের অপূর্ণ ইচ্ছা প্রকাশ। সঠিক: Had I seen you before!

options.text: Going to the book fair, I bought a number of books.

options.text: Is your payment found too little by you?

entries.correct_answer: ক) Is your payment found too little to you?
entries.explanation: Active object 'your payment' (singular) → passive subject → verb 'is'। NTRCA-স্বীকৃত preposition 'to' (মনে হওয়া/বিবেচনা অর্থে)।

entries.question_text: There is little milk in the glass. (Interrogative)

options.text: Is there little milk in the glass?

options.text: Isn't there any milk in the glass?

entries.correct_answer: গ) Is there any milk in the glass?
entries.explanation: 'Little' negative-বোধক (প্রায় নেই) → Interrogative-এ 'any' দিয়ে প্রশ্ন করা হয়। সঠিক: Is there any milk in the glass?

entries.question_text: I know him better than you. (Positive)

options.label: ক
options.text: You do not know him as good as I.

options.label: খ
options.text: You do not know him as well as I.

options.text: You do not know him as well as me.

options.text: You do not know him as good as me.

entries.correct_answer: খ) You do not know him as well as I.
entries.explanation: Comparative 'better' → Positive 'as well as' (adverb 'well'-এর positive)। তুলনার দুই পক্ষ subject হওয়ায় 'I' (nominative case), 'me' নয়।

entries.question_text: I am sure that he (pass) the examination.
entries.options_raw: ক) will pass খ) passed গ) will be passed ঘ) pass
entries.explanation: 'Be sure that' এর পর ভবিষ্যত-অভিব্যক্তি — future indefinite 'will pass'।

entries.question_text: Walk carefully lest ________.
entries.options_raw: ক) you will fall খ) you should stumble গ) you would have fallen ঘ) you might lose the way
entries.explanation: 'Lest' conjunction-এর পর subject + should + bare infinitive। 'Stumble' মানে হোঁচট খাওয়া — সাবধানে হাঁটার প্রেক্ষাপটে যথার্থ।

entries.question_text: People (talk) his courage even after his death.
entries.options_raw: ক) talk of খ) talk গ) will talk ঘ) talks of
entries.explanation: 'Talk of' phrasal verb — কারো প্রশংসা/আলোচনা করা। Subject 'people' (plural) → verb 'talk of'। Universal truth-এ present indefinite।

entries.question_text: Three-fourths of the work ______ finished.
entries.options_raw: ক) have been খ) is গ) are ঘ) has been
entries.explanation: 'Fraction of + uncountable noun' → verb of-এর পরবর্তী noun-এর সঙ্গে মিলবে। 'Work' uncountable, তাই singular verb 'has been'।

entries.question_text: We felt very tired. The word 'tired' used in the sentence is ______
entries.options_raw: ক) adjective খ) noun গ) verb ঘ) none
entries.explanation: 'Feel' linking verb; পরে বসা 'tired' subject-এর অবস্থা বোঝাচ্ছে — subject complement/adjective। অনুরূপ: seem, appear, become ইত্যাদি।

entries.question_text: The verb of the word 'beautiful' is _____.
entries.options_raw: ক) beauty খ) beautify গ) beautification ঘ) beautifully
entries.explanation: Beautiful (adj.) → Beautify (verb, সৌন্দর্যবর্ধন করা)। Beauty (noun), beautification (noun), beautifully (adv.)।

entries.question_text: The synonym of the word 'huge' is _____.
entries.options_raw: ক) sanctified খ) tiny গ) colossal ঘ) momentary
entries.explanation: 'Huge' মানে বিশাল/বৃহৎ; সমার্থক 'colossal' (gigantic, immense)। 'Tiny' বিপরীত (ক্ষুদ্র)।

entries.question_text: The antonym of the word 'unique' is _______.
entries.options_raw: ক) popular খ) common গ) distinctive ঘ) deciduous
entries.explanation: 'Unique' মানে অদ্বিতীয়/অনন্য; বিপরীত 'common' — সাধারণ। Distinctive সমার্থক; deciduous মানে পত্রঝরা গাছ।

options.text: She had faith on & hopes for the future.

options.text: She had faith & hopes for the future.

options.text: She had faith & hopes in the future.

options.label: ঘ
options.text: She had faith in & hopes for the future.

entries.options_raw: ক) She had faith on & hopes for the future. খ) She had faith & hopes for the future. গ) She had faith & hopes in the future. ঘ) She had faith in & hopes for the future.
entries.correct_answer: ঘ) She had faith in & hopes for the future.
entries.explanation: প্রতিটি noun-এর নিজস্ব preposition বজায় রাখতে হয় — 'faith in' এবং 'hope for'। সঠিক: She had faith in and hopes for the future.

entries.question_text: She argued ____ me about the marriage.
entries.options_raw: ক) with খ) for গ) to ঘ) from
entries.explanation: 'Argue with someone about something' — নির্দিষ্ট collocation (কারো সঙ্গে কোনো বিষয়ে তর্ক করা)।

entries.question_text: Choose the appropriate meaning of the idiom 'Swan Song'.
entries.options_raw: ক) first work খ) last work গ) middle work ঘ) early work
entries.explanation: 'Swan Song' idiom — কারো শেষ কর্ম/পরিবেশনা। প্রচলিত বিশ্বাস, রাজহাঁস মৃত্যুর ঠিক আগেই সবচেয়ে সুন্দর গান গায়; সেই ধারণা থেকে idiom-এর উৎপত্তি।

entries.question_text: শিশুটি হাসতে হাসতে আমার কাছে এলো —

options.text: The baby come to me by laughing
